boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Minnesota-Twin Cities
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food stops with publicly listed late hours, centered on Dinkytown and extending to Minneapolis options for a later meal or pickup.

cards.title: Frank & Andrea Dinkytown
cards.subtitle: 1235 4th St SE, Minneapolis
cards.notes: Check the day before heading over: the Dinkytown location lists 2 a.m. closes Monday–Wednesday and 3 a.m. closes Thursday–Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A Dinkytown pizza and cheesesteak counter with especially late listed hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Frank & Andrea’s official site lists its Dinkytown location at 1235 4th St SE and closing times as late as 3 a.m. Thursday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Frank & Andrea — Dinkytown location and hours
cards.access_notes: Officially listed hours: Mon–Wed 11 a.m.–2 a.m.; Thu–Sat 11 a.m.–3 a.m.; Sun 11 a.m.–midnight.

cards.title: Raising Cane's Dinkytown
cards.subtitle: 302 15th Ave SE, Minneapolis
cards.notes: Use the location’s day-by-day schedule before a late pickup; its Thursday through Saturday dining hours are listed through 3 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A Dinkytown chicken-finger restaurant with late weekend hours on its official locator.
cards.evidence_claim: Raising Cane’s official Dinkytown page lists dine-in hours until 3 a.m. Thursday, Friday, and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Raising Cane's Dinkytown
cards.access_notes: Officially listed dine-in hours: 10 a.m.–midnight Sun–Wed; 10 a.m.–3 a.m. Thu–Sat.

cards.title: Mesa Pizza Dinkytown
cards.subtitle: 1323 4th St SE, Minneapolis
cards.notes: Plan for a late slice or pickup on Thursday through Saturday, and allow for the posted notice that the kitchen may stop before the store closes.
cards.short_summary: A Dinkytown pizza shop whose official schedule reaches 2 a.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Mesa Pizza’s official Dinkytown page lists hours until 1 a.m. Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Mesa Pizza Dinkytown
cards.access_notes: Officially listed hours: Sun–Wed 11 a.m.–11 p.m.; Thu 11 a.m.–1 a.m.; Fri–Sat 11 a.m.–2 a.m. The site says the kitchen closes 15–30 minutes earlier.

cards.title: Chipotle Mexican Grill Dinkytown
cards.subtitle: 1421 4th St SE, Minneapolis
cards.notes: For an earlier late-night option on the Dinkytown corridor, confirm the restaurant’s current 11 p.m. closing time before placing an order.
cards.short_summary: A Dinkytown burrito-and-bowl stop officially listed until 11 p.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Chipotle’s official Dinkytown location page lists restaurant hours of 10:45 a.m. to 11 p.m. every day.
cards.source_title: Chipotle Mexican Grill — Dinkytown
cards.access_notes: Officially listed restaurant hours: 10:45 a.m.–11 p.m., Monday through Sunday.

cards.title: Pizza Lucé Seward
cards.subtitle: 2200 E Franklin Ave, Minneapolis
cards.notes: Use the Seward location’s ordering channel when later service matters: its page separately lists delivery and pickup through 1 a.m. every day.
cards.short_summary: A Minneapolis Pizza Lucé location with delivery and pickup listed until 1 a.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Lucé’s official Seward page lists delivery and pickup until 1 a.m. every day, with dine-in until midnight.
cards.source_title: Pizza Lucé Seward
cards.access_notes: Officially listed daily hours: delivery and pickup 11 a.m.–1 a.m.; dine-in 11 a.m.–midnight.

cards.title: Pizza Lucé Uptown
cards.subtitle: 3200 Lyndale Ave S, Minneapolis
cards.notes: For a later pickup or delivery, use the Uptown location’s schedule rather than assuming its dining-room hours match; the two are listed separately.
cards.short_summary: An Uptown Pizza Lucé location with pickup and delivery extending past midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Lucé’s official Uptown page lists delivery and pickup until 2 a.m. most nights and 2:30 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Pizza Lucé Uptown
cards.access_notes: Officially listed delivery/pickup: until 2 a.m. Sun–Thu and 2:30 a.m. Fri–Sat; dine-in is listed until midnight.

cards.title: Leaning Tower of Pizza
cards.subtitle: 2324 Lyndale Ave S, Minneapolis
cards.notes: Check the current location page before traveling to Uptown; it lists service until 2 a.m. every day and gives the full street address.
cards.short_summary: An Uptown pizza restaurant that publicly lists a 2 a.m. close every night.
cards.evidence_claim: Leaning Tower of Pizza’s official site lists its Minneapolis location at 2324 Lyndale Ave S and hours until 2 a.m. daily.
cards.source_title: Leaning Tower of Pizza — hours and location
cards.access_notes: Officially listed hours: 4 p.m.–2 a.m. Monday–Friday; noon–2 a.m. Saturday and Sunday.

cards.title: The Nicollet Diner
cards.subtitle: 1333 Nicollet Mall, Minneapolis
cards.notes: Keep this downtown diner in mind for a meal outside ordinary closing windows; its own site says it operates 24 hours a day, every day.
cards.short_summary: A downtown diner whose official site advertises 24-hour daily service.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nicollet Diner’s official website states that it is open 24 hours a day, every day, at 1333 Nicollet Mall.
cards.source_title: The Nicollet Diner
cards.access_notes: Official site states: “24 Hours a Day, Every Day.” Confirm any service details directly with the diner before going.

cards.title: Hard Times Cafe
cards.subtitle: 1821 Riverside Ave, Minneapolis
cards.notes: For a Cedar-Riverside stop, use the current listing as a guide and arrive before midnight; the visitor bureau lists daily hours from 8 a.m. to midnight.
cards.short_summary: A Cedar-Riverside vegetarian café publicly listed as open until midnight daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Meet Minneapolis lists Hard Times Cafe in Cedar-Riverside as open from 8 a.m. to midnight.
cards.source_title: Meet Minneapolis — A Night Owl’s Guide to Minneapolis
cards.access_notes: Meet Minneapolis lists Hard Times Cafe hours as 8 a.m.–midnight. Confirm directly before traveling, as hours can change.

cards.title: Nightingale
cards.subtitle: 2551 Lyndale Ave S, Minneapolis
cards.notes: If you are heading toward Lyndale, use the restaurant’s stated kitchen cutoff rather than its room closing time: food is listed through midnight daily.
cards.short_summary: A Lyndale restaurant whose official page lists a midnight kitchen close every day.
cards.evidence_claim: Nightingale’s official site lists daily hours from 5 p.m. to 1 a.m. and states that its kitchen is open until midnight.
cards.source_title: Nightingale — hours and location
cards.access_notes: Officially listed hours: 5 p.m.–1 a.m. Sunday–Saturday; the site specifies that the kitchen is open until midnight.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus spaces for studying, collaborating, making, or taking a break between classes.

cards.title: Whole Music Club
cards.subtitle: Coffman Memorial Union basement, East Bank
cards.notes: Check whether the room is hosting a concert; when it is not, use its tables and couches for an individual session or to spread out with classmates.
cards.short_summary: A concert venue that also opens as a public study space when not in use for performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Unions & Activities identifies the Whole Music Club as a Coffman basement study space with tables and couches when it is not being used for concerts.
cards.source_title: Coffman Memorial Union | Student Unions and Activities
cards.access_notes: Inside Coffman Memorial Union; public study use is available when the venue is not in use for concerts. Check current building hours.

cards.title: Goldy's Gameroom
cards.subtitle: Coffman Memorial Union basement, East Bank
cards.notes: Bring work that suits a livelier room: the space has music, food, tables, and chairs, so it works for a change of pace from a quiet floor.
cards.short_summary: A basement union room with study tables in a more animated setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Unions & Activities states that Goldy's Gameroom offers music, food, tables, and chairs for studying.
cards.source_title: Coffman Memorial Union | Student Unions and Activities
cards.access_notes: Located in the Coffman basement. Check current Coffman building hours before going.

cards.title: The Cube
cards.subtitle: Coffman Memorial Union ground floor, East Bank
cards.notes: Set up at a table or couch near the west end of the ground floor, beside Starbucks and the University of Minnesota Bookstore.
cards.short_summary: A ground-floor Coffman seating area with tables and couches.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Unions & Activities describes The Cube as a west-end Coffman ground-floor space with tables and couches for studying.
cards.source_title: Coffman Memorial Union | Student Unions and Activities
cards.access_notes: Located on Coffman's ground floor; this shared/public space cannot be reserved. Check current building hours.

cards.title: East Fireplace Lounge
cards.subtitle: Coffman Memorial Union first floor, East Bank
cards.notes: Use the first-floor lounge for a seated work session, and bring a charger: Student Unions & Activities notes plentiful places to plug in and recharge.
cards.short_summary: One of Coffman's first-floor fireplace lounges with seating and power access.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Unions & Activities lists the East Fireplace Lounge as a first-floor study space with comfortable chairs and places to plug in.
cards.source_title: Coffman Memorial Union | Student Unions and Activities
cards.access_notes: On Coffman's first floor; fireplace lounges are shared/public spaces and cannot be reserved. Check current building hours.

cards.title: West Fireplace Lounge
cards.subtitle: Coffman Memorial Union first floor, East Bank
cards.notes: Meet a classmate or settle into a chair in this first-floor lounge; nearby vending machines offer a practical break without leaving the building.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor Coffman lounge with seating, power access, and nearby vending.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Unions & Activities identifies the West Fireplace Lounge as a first-floor study lounge with comfortable chairs, power access, and nearby vending machines.
cards.source_title: Coffman Memorial Union | Student Unions and Activities
cards.access_notes: On Coffman's first floor; fireplace lounges are shared/public spaces and cannot be reserved. Check current building hours.

cards.title: Fountain Terrace
cards.subtitle: Coffman Memorial Union south end, East Bank
cards.notes: On warmer days, take your reading or low-key group work outside to the terrace tables and benches around the Pietro Tacca fountain.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor Coffman terrace with tables, benches, and the Pietro Tacca fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Unions & Activities describes Fountain Terrace as an outdoor study space during warmer months, with tables and benches around the Pietro Tacca fountain.
cards.source_title: Coffman Memorial Union | Student Unions and Activities
cards.access_notes: At the south end of Coffman; outdoor study use is seasonal and weather-dependent.

cards.title: Mississippi Lounge
cards.subtitle: Coffman Memorial Union third floor, East Bank
cards.notes: Head to the third floor for river-facing seating; confirm that no private event has reserved the adjoining Mississippi Room before relying on it.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor Coffman lounge with views of the Mississippi River and Fountain Terrace.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Unions & Activities says the Mississippi Lounge has views of the Mississippi River and Fountain Terrace and is open to students when not reserved for a private event.
cards.source_title: Coffman Memorial Union | Student Unions and Activities
cards.access_notes: Third floor of Coffman. Open to students when not reserved for a private event; check current building hours.

cards.title: The Toaster Innovation Hub
cards.subtitle: Walter Library basement, East Bank
cards.notes: Use the open study area for project planning, or reserve a meeting, workshop, or event space through the Libraries' Toaster process.
cards.short_summary: A Walter Library collaboration hub with open study and reservable spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Minnesota Libraries states that The Toaster in Walter Library is free for UMN students and includes open study plus reservable meeting, workshop, and event spaces.
cards.source_title: Spaces | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: In Walter Library's basement. UMN library access requires a U Card; some public access is available by appointment.

cards.title: Walter Library Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Walter Library, East Bank
cards.notes: Drop in to make a prototype or try equipment such as a 3D printer, sewing machine, button makers, or VR headsets; all skill levels are welcome.
cards.short_summary: A student-run, hands-on making space inside Walter Library.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Minnesota Libraries describes Walter Library's Makerspace as a free-to-use, student-run space with hands-on tools and materials for all majors, years, and skill levels.
cards.source_title: Walter Library | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: Inside Walter Library. A U Card is required for library access; some public access is available by appointment.

cards.title: Northrop Study Lounges
cards.subtitle: Northrop floors 1–3, East Bank
cards.notes: Choose an east- or west-side lounge on floors one through three for a first-come study session, then connect a laptop to the monitor for collaborative work.
cards.short_summary: Six first-come student lounges in Northrop with tables, seating, power, and HDMI-enabled monitors.
cards.evidence_claim: Northrop states that its six student study lounges are first-come, first-served and offer natural light, tables, seating, power, Wi-Fi, and monitors for collaborative presentations.
cards.source_title: Study Lounges | Northrop
cards.access_notes: Located at the southeast and southwest corners of Northrop floors one through three; first-come, first-served.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten named Twin Cities destinations where UMN students can spend time with art, exhibits, nature, or friends without admission or a purchase.

cards.title: Browse the Weisman galleries
cards.subtitle: East Bank, University of Minnesota Twin Cities
cards.notes: Meet at the museum entrance, move through the galleries at your own pace, and use the building’s riverfront setting as a natural conversation break.
cards.short_summary: A campus art-museum visit with free admission for everyone.
cards.evidence_claim: Weisman Art Museum states that it offers free admission to all.
cards.source_title: Make a Gift | Weisman Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Open to students and the general public; check the museum’s current visitor information before going.

cards.title: Walk the Bell Museum galleries
cards.subtitle: 2088 Larpenteur Ave W, Saint Paul
cards.notes: Bring a valid student ID, reserve or ask at arrival as directed, then explore the natural-history galleries together without adding a planetarium ticket.
cards.short_summary: UMN students can enter the museum galleries free with student ID.
cards.evidence_claim: Bell Museum lists Museum Gallery Admission for UMN students with student ID as free; planetarium shows cost extra.
cards.source_title: Plan your visit! | Bell Museum
cards.access_notes: Valid UMN student ID is required for free gallery admission. Planetarium admission is not included.

cards.title: Take a garden walk at the Arboretum
cards.subtitle: University of Minnesota Landscape Arboretum, Chaska
cards.notes: Call ahead to book the required student ticket, bring your U Card and UMN email access, then choose a garden or trail for an unhurried group walk.
cards.short_summary: A student-ID-supported garden and trail outing at the university’s Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arboretum states that current University of Minnesota students receive complimentary admission and must call to book tickets.
cards.source_title: Ticket Details | University of Minnesota Landscape Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Current UMN students must call 612-301-6775 to book complimentary admission; bring required student credentials.

cards.title: Make a self-guided sculpture loop
cards.subtitle: 726 Vineland Place, Minneapolis
cards.notes: Pick a few works to discuss, pause at Spoonbridge and Cherry, and use the free digital guide if your group wants artwork context while walking.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor public-art walk with no ticket or admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Walker states that the Minneapolis Sculpture Garden requires no tickets and is always free to the public.
cards.source_title: Minneapolis Sculpture Garden | Walker Art Center
cards.access_notes: Open daily, 6 a.m.–midnight year-round according to the Walker; parking may have a charge.

cards.title: See an Andersen Library exhibition
cards.subtitle: West Bank; library exhibitions
cards.notes: Check what is currently installed, then use the gallery and atrium displays as a low-key stop before or after time on the West Bank.
cards.short_summary: Free library exhibitions in the university’s archives and special-collections building.
cards.evidence_claim: UMN Libraries says all Libraries exhibitions are open to the public and free of charge, and identifies Andersen Library exhibition spaces.
cards.source_title: Libraries exhibit policy | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: UMN Libraries says its buildings are U Card-only; active UMN students can use their U Card. Others need an appointment.

cards.title: Look through a Rapson Hall exhibit
cards.subtitle: Rapson Hall; library exhibitions
cards.notes: Coordinate a quick meet-up in Rapson Hall, look over the library’s exhibit area, and leave time to compare details that caught each person’s eye.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost campus exhibit stop inside Rapson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: UMN Libraries says all Libraries exhibitions are open to the public and free of charge, including exhibitions at the Architecture and Landscape Architecture Library in Rapson Hall.
cards.source_title: Libraries exhibit policy | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: UMN Libraries says its buildings are U Card-only; active UMN students can use their U Card. Confirm current displays before visiting.

cards.title: Visit a Vincent Hall library exhibit
cards.subtitle: Vincent Hall; library exhibitions
cards.notes: Use the exhibit cases as a brief study-break destination, then continue the hang with a walk across Northrop Mall or nearby campus paths.
cards.short_summary: Free exhibition viewing in the Mathematics Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UMN Libraries says all Libraries exhibitions are open to the public and free of charge, including exhibitions at the Mathematics Library in Vincent Hall.
cards.source_title: Libraries exhibit policy | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: UMN Libraries says its buildings are U Card-only; active UMN students can use their U Card. Confirm current displays before visiting.

cards.title: Check out a Ferguson Hall exhibit
cards.subtitle: Ferguson Hall; library exhibitions
cards.notes: Stop in between classes or rehearsals, spend a few minutes with the display cases, and use the visit as an easy starting point for a campus walk.
cards.short_summary: A free exhibit-focused visit to the Music Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UMN Libraries says all Libraries exhibitions are open to the public and free of charge, including exhibitions at the Music Library in Ferguson Hall.
cards.source_title: Libraries exhibit policy | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: UMN Libraries says its buildings are U Card-only; active UMN students can use their U Card. Confirm current displays before visiting.

cards.title: Browse a Hodson Hall exhibit
cards.subtitle: Hodson Hall; library exhibitions
cards.notes: Choose a display to inspect together, trade observations, and pair the visit with a daylight walk through the nearby St. Paul campus landscape.
cards.short_summary: Free exhibition viewing at the Natural Resources Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UMN Libraries says all Libraries exhibitions are open to the public and free of charge, including exhibitions at the Natural Resources Library in Hodson Hall.
cards.source_title: Libraries exhibit policy | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: UMN Libraries says its buildings are U Card-only; active UMN students can use their U Card. Confirm current displays before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Wangensteen Historical Library of Biology and Medicine
cards.title: Explore a Wangensteen library exhibit
cards.subtitle: Phillips-Wangensteen Building; library exhibitions
cards.notes: Plan a focused visit to the historical-library display area, read labels together, and keep the hang simple by discussing one item each person noticed.
cards.short_summary: A free exhibition stop in the historical biology and medicine library.
cards.evidence_claim: UMN Libraries says all Libraries exhibitions are open to the public and free of charge, including exhibitions at the Wangensteen Historical Library of Biology and Medicine.
cards.source_title: Libraries exhibit policy | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: UMN Libraries says its buildings are U Card-only; active UMN students can use their U Card. Confirm current displays before visiting.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented University Libraries study environments across East Bank, West Bank, and the Saint Paul campus.

cards.title: Walter Library 206
cards.subtitle: Walter Library · East Bank
cards.notes: Use the mix of tables, chairs, and individual desks to switch between solo reading and a small working session.
cards.short_summary: A large East Bank open-study area with natural light and varied seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Walter Library 206 is an open study space with capacity 172, natural light, tables and chairs, individual desks, and a low-hum noise level.
cards.source_title: Walter Library 206 | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: A U Card is required to access University of Minnesota Libraries locations; use during Walter Library building hours.

cards.title: Walter Library Sub-basement Floor
cards.subtitle: Walter Library · East Bank
cards.notes: Settle into the tables or lounge seating in the stacks when you need a quiet setting for reading or written work.
cards.short_summary: Quiet open study seating among Walter Library’s stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: Walter Library’s sub-basement is an open study space with tables, chairs, lounge seating, capacity 30, and a quiet noise level.
cards.source_title: Walter Library - Sub-basement floor | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: A U Card is required to access University of Minnesota Libraries locations; use during Walter Library building hours.

cards.title: Walter Library 204F
cards.subtitle: Walter Library · East Bank
cards.notes: Reserve this four-person glass-walled room when your group needs a whiteboard and an enclosed place to work together.
cards.short_summary: A reservable four-person group room with a fixed whiteboard.
cards.evidence_claim: Walter Library 204F is a reservable study room for four with natural light, tables and chairs, a fixed whiteboard, and a low-hum noise level.
cards.source_title: Walter Library 204F | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required; a U Card is required for library access.

cards.title: Wilson Library Second Floor
cards.subtitle: Wilson Library · West Bank
cards.notes: Choose a table, chair, or lounge seat and keep the session quiet; the listed area supports a range of seating styles.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, high-capacity Wilson Library study area with lounge seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Wilson Library’s second-floor open study space has capacity 100, tables and chairs, lounge seating, and a quiet noise level.
cards.source_title: Wilson Library - 2nd floor | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: A U Card is required to access University of Minnesota Libraries locations; use during Wilson Library building hours.

cards.title: Wilson Library Fourth Floor
cards.subtitle: Wilson Library · West Bank
cards.notes: Bring reading or laptop work to the fourth floor and use its naturally lit tables, chairs, or lounge seating.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, naturally lit fourth-floor study area.
cards.evidence_claim: Wilson Library’s fourth-floor open study space has capacity 20, natural light, tables and chairs, lounge seating, and a quiet noise level.
cards.source_title: Wilson Library - 4th floor | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: A U Card is required to access University of Minnesota Libraries locations; use during Wilson Library building hours.

cards.title: Wilson Library 301B
cards.subtitle: Wilson Library · West Bank
cards.notes: Plan an unplugged reading session here: the room is designated deep quiet, with no laptop or cell-phone use.
cards.short_summary: A naturally lit, device-free deep-quiet room for individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Wilson Library 301B is an open study space for individual study with a large window, tables and chairs, natural light, and a quiet noise level; laptops and cell phones are not allowed.
cards.source_title: Wilson Library 301B | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: A U Card is required to access University of Minnesota Libraries locations. Do not use laptops or cell phones in this space.

cards.title: Wilson Research Collaboration Studio
cards.subtitle: Wilson Library · West Bank
cards.notes: Bring a project group and use the mobile whiteboards and display monitors to map ideas, share screens, or review drafts.
cards.short_summary: An open collaborative space with whiteboards, displays, and large windows.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wilson Research Collaboration Studio is an open study space for collaborative and group work with mobile whiteboards, mobile and fixed display monitors, natural light, and capacity 60.
cards.source_title: Wilson Library - Research Collaboration Studio | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: A U Card is required to access University of Minnesota Libraries locations; use during Wilson Library building hours.

cards.title: Wilson Library 423
cards.subtitle: Wilson Library · West Bank
cards.notes: Reserve this single-person room when you need an individual desk, natural light, and a quieter enclosed study setting.
cards.short_summary: A reservable one-person study room on Wilson’s fourth floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Wilson Library 423 is a reservable, quiet study room for one with natural light and an individual desk.
cards.source_title: Wilson Library 423 | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required; a U Card is required for library access.

cards.title: Magrath Library First Floor
cards.subtitle: Magrath Library · Saint Paul Campus
cards.notes: Use the first-floor carrels, tables, or soft seating for individual work, then shift seats if your task changes.
cards.short_summary: Naturally lit Saint Paul campus seating for individual or group quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: Magrath Library’s first-floor open study space has capacity 15, natural light, tables and chairs, individual desks, and a low-hum noise level.
cards.source_title: Magrath Library - 1st floor | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: A U Card is required to access University of Minnesota Libraries locations; use during Magrath Library building hours.

cards.title: Health Sciences Education Center Room 5-105
cards.subtitle: Health Sciences Education Center · East Bank
cards.notes: Arrive during building hours and select furniture that fits the task; movable whiteboards, wireless access, and power are available.
cards.short_summary: A first-come, first-served quiet study area with flexible furniture.
cards.evidence_claim: Health Sciences Education Center room 5-105 is a large open quiet-study area available first come, first served during building hours, with movable whiteboards, wireless access, and power.
cards.source_title: Study spaces | Health Sciences Libraries
cards.access_notes: Available first come, first served during building hours; a U Card is required for University of Minnesota library access.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named stops on campus-adjacent Dinkytown, Riverside Avenue, Cedar Avenue, and South Fourth Street corridors, each with a directly sourced reason to go.

cards.title: A breakfast stop on 14th
cards.subtitle: 14th Avenue SE corridor, between 4th and 5th streets
cards.notes: Use the official directions to find this Dinkytown breakfast counter on 14th Avenue SE; check its current closing-day notice before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A specifically located breakfast counter in historic Dinkytown.
cards.evidence_claim: Al's Breakfast says it is in historic Dinkytown on 14th Avenue SE between 4th and 5th streets and lists its Minneapolis address as 413 14th Ave SE.
cards.source_title: How to Find Us | Al's Breakfast
cards.access_notes: The official page lists service hours and several annual closure dates; verify the page before visiting.

cards.title: Browse upstairs books
cards.subtitle: 4th Street SE corridor, Dinkytown
cards.notes: Go upstairs at 1316 4th Street SE and allow time to browse; the shop’s contact page posts distinct weekday and weekend hours.
cards.short_summary: An upstairs bookshop with published hours on the 4th Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Book House in Dinkytown lists its upstairs address as 1316 4th St SE, Minneapolis, along with weekday and weekend hours.
cards.source_title: Contact | The Book House in Dinkytown
cards.access_notes: The shop is upstairs; consult its contact page for the current day’s hours.

cards.title: Use a public library branch
cards.subtitle: 4th Street SE corridor, Dinkytown
cards.notes: Bring a library card if you plan to borrow materials, or use this 4th Street SE branch as a public indoor stop during its listed hours.
cards.short_summary: A county library branch directly on the Dinkytown 4th Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Hennepin County lists Arvonne Fraser Library at 1222 4th Street Southeast in Minneapolis and publishes its weekly hours.
cards.source_title: Library locations | Hennepin County
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by day and the branch is listed as closed Sundays; confirm the county schedule before visiting.

cards.title: A Mediterranean menu stop
cards.subtitle: 14th Avenue SE corridor, Dinkytown
cards.notes: Check the restaurant’s menu before you go and use its Dinkytown location as a 14th Avenue SE food stop near the 4th Street junction.
cards.short_summary: A Dinkytown restaurant whose official page identifies Mediterranean and Middle Eastern dishes.
cards.evidence_claim: Wally's official site identifies the Dinkytown restaurant as being on 4th Street SE in Minneapolis and lists falafel, hummus, shawirma, kabobs, and teas.
cards.source_title: About Us | Wally's Falafel and Hummus
cards.access_notes: Menu items and availability can change; review the restaurant’s current information before ordering.

cards.title: A 4th Street food address
cards.subtitle: 4th Street SE corridor, Dinkytown
cards.notes: Use the Dinkytown association’s address listing to locate this Suite A food stop, then check the business directly for current ordering details.
cards.short_summary: A named restaurant listing at 1421 4th Street SE.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dinkytown Business Association directory lists Boba X Ramen at 1421 4th Street SE, Suite A.
cards.source_title: Dinkytown Business Association Directory
cards.access_notes: The association directory supplies the location; confirm current service details with the business before a visit.

cards.title: Explore an Ethiopian menu
cards.subtitle: Riverside Avenue corridor, Cedar-Riverside
cards.notes: Find Dilla’s at 1813 Riverside Avenue and review its menu first if you are planning a meal with a group or dietary preferences.
cards.short_summary: A Riverside Avenue Ethiopian restaurant with a directly published address.
cards.evidence_claim: Dilla's Ethiopian Restaurant publishes its address as 1813 Riverside Ave, Minneapolis, MN 55454.
cards.source_title: Dilla Ethiopian Restaurant | Contact
cards.access_notes: The restaurant’s official contact page provides the address and online ordering link; verify service details before visiting.

cards.title: A Riverside Avenue café
cards.subtitle: Riverside Avenue corridor, Cedar-Riverside
cards.notes: Use the City’s license record to confirm the Riverside Avenue address, then check the café directly for current food service and access details.
cards.short_summary: A named café at 1821 Riverside Avenue in Cedar-Riverside.
cards.evidence_claim: A City of Minneapolis license record identifies Hard Times Cafe at 1821 Riverside Ave in the Cedar-Riverside neighborhood.
cards.source_title: Hard Times Cafe Street Cafe License Record | City of Minneapolis
cards.access_notes: This source verifies the location; contact the café directly for current hours and offerings.

cards.title: See the global-music calendar
cards.subtitle: Cedar Avenue South corridor, Cedar-Riverside
cards.notes: Review the current event calendar and the specific event’s admission details before going to this nonprofit venue at 416 Cedar Avenue South.
cards.short_summary: A Cedar-Riverside nonprofit presenting global music and dance.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cedar states that its mission includes presenting global music and dance and lists its location as 416 Cedar Avenue South in Minneapolis.
cards.source_title: The Cedar Cultural Center
cards.access_notes: Admission, age guidance, and schedules are event-specific; check the listing before attending.

cards.title: A theatre-in-the-round performance
cards.subtitle: Cedar Avenue South corridor, West Bank Theatre District
cards.notes: Check the production page for content and ticket details, then plan for the theatre at 245 Cedar Avenue on the West Bank corridor.
cards.short_summary: A community theatre located between the University’s main campus and downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Theatre in the Round says it is in the West Bank Theatre District, between the University of Minnesota main campus and downtown, at 245 Cedar Avenue.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Theatre in the Round Players
cards.access_notes: Show times, ticketing, and content notices are production-specific; review the theatre’s current visit page before attending.

cards.title: The historic Firehouse venue
cards.subtitle: South Fourth Street corridor, West Bank
cards.notes: Look for public performances or community programming at the Firehouse and confirm the current event’s access details before traveling to South Fourth Street.
cards.short_summary: A theatre organization based at 1501 South Fourth Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Mixed Blood identifies its location as 1501 South Fourth Street, Minneapolis, and says it uses theatre to advance equity and build community.
cards.source_title: Contact | Mixed Blood
cards.access_notes: Confirm whether a public event is scheduled and review that event’s admission and age information before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Minnesota–Twin Cities traditions, from the Rouser and Block M to annual campus gatherings.

cards.title: Rub Goldy’s Teeth
cards.subtitle: Goldy Gopher statue outside Coffman Memorial Union
cards.notes: Find the Goldy statue outside Coffman and rub its teeth as part of the campus good-luck ritual before a test or athletic event.
cards.short_summary: A newer campus ritual centered on the Goldy statue’s prominent teeth.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says many students rub the Goldy statue’s teeth for good luck before a big test or athletic event.
cards.source_title: Big Ten | Office of Admissions
cards.access_notes: The source places the statue outside Coffman Memorial Union; confirm building access separately.

cards.title: Sing the Minnesota Rouser
cards.subtitle: University fight song
cards.notes: Listen for the Rouser at a Gopher sporting event and join the refrain when the band leads the crowd in the school song.
cards.short_summary: The University’s 1909 contest-winning fight song remains a core Gopher refrain.
cards.evidence_claim: The University’s marching-band history documents the Rouser’s 1909 contest origin and its regular use over generations.
cards.source_title: Minnesota Rouser | College of Liberal Arts
cards.access_notes: Typically encountered at athletic and marching-band events; event admission policies vary.

cards.title: Answer with Ski-U-Mah
cards.subtitle: Gopher rally cry
cards.notes: Notice the “Ski-U-Mah” call within the Rouser and at spirit occasions; use it as a campus rally cry, not as a claim about origin.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive Gopher exclamation embedded in the University’s fight-song tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: The University’s published Rouser lyrics include the repeated “Ski-U-Mah” rally cry.
cards.source_title: Minnesota Rouser | College of Liberal Arts
cards.access_notes: No separate access is required to learn the phrase; its public use occurs at spirit events.

cards.title: Spot the Block M
cards.subtitle: Minnesota Marching Band halftime formation
cards.notes: At a home football game or band program, watch for the Marching Band’s Block M formation and its visual link to University identity.
cards.short_summary: The Marching Band’s signature letter formation dates to its first halftime show.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says the Marching Band included the first Block M in its 1910 halftime show and that it is now a University symbol.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions | College of Liberal Arts
cards.access_notes: Shown during selected band performances and home football events; consult the relevant event listing.

cards.title: Mark Homecoming Week
cards.subtitle: Annual fall campus tradition
cards.notes: Use the annual Homecoming schedule to choose a campus event, then take in the broader week of Gopher spirit with alumni and students.
cards.short_summary: A campus-wide fall tradition with roots at Minnesota in 1914.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes Homecoming as a Minnesota tradition since 1914 and lists its campus spirit events.
cards.source_title: Big Ten | Office of Admissions
cards.access_notes: Homecoming 2026 is scheduled for October 19–24; individual events can have separate access rules.

cards.title: Line Up for the Homecoming Parade
cards.subtitle: Annual parade during Homecoming
cards.notes: Check the official route and time, then watch campus groups, alumni, and the Marching Band take part in the Homecoming Parade.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing Homecoming gathering that showcases University spirit in public.
cards.evidence_claim: The University calls the Homecoming Parade one of its longest-standing and most attended traditions; the 2026 parade is set for October 23.
cards.source_title: 2026 Homecoming Parade | University of Minnesota
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for Friday, October 23, 2026 at 6:30 p.m.; check the official page for route and updates.

cards.title: Follow Homecoming Royalty
cards.subtitle: Student ambassador court and royal selection
cards.notes: Read the current Homecoming Royalty materials to see how court members represent the University throughout Homecoming Week.
cards.short_summary: A long-running recognition tradition now framed around student representation.
cards.evidence_claim: The University states that Homecoming Royalty is a long-standing tradition and selects two court members as Homecoming Royals.
cards.source_title: Homecoming Royalty | University of Minnesota
cards.access_notes: Applications and selection details are seasonal; use the official Homecoming page for current participation information.

cards.title: Begin at New Student Convocation
cards.subtitle: Official welcome for incoming students
cards.notes: If you are a new student, attend Convocation with your class and look for the academic-regalia ceremony that formally opens the year.
cards.short_summary: The University’s formal incoming-class welcome brings new students together before the academic year begins.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes New Student Convocation as its official welcome to the incoming class and an annual tradition.
cards.source_title: A tradition of pride, purpose, and community at Convocation | Brief
cards.access_notes: Intended for incoming students during Welcome Week; attendance and logistics are communicated by the University.

cards.title: Close the Year at Spring Jam
cards.subtitle: Student-planned end-of-year campus festival
cards.notes: Check the official Spring Jam program for performances and activities, then choose an all-ages area rather than the separately restricted beer garden.
cards.short_summary: A student-planned campus festival that marks the end of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes Spring Jam as a student-planned campus festival celebrating the end of the school year.
cards.source_title: About Spring Jam | University of Minnesota
cards.access_notes: The 2026 event is listed for April 25 at Coffman Memorial Union; use all-ages festival areas and avoid the 21+ beer garden.

cards.title: Hear the Indoor Concert
cards.subtitle: Annual Northrop Marching Band concert
cards.notes: Reserve or obtain event information through Northrop, then experience the Marching Band’s annual indoor performance and Goldy appearance.
cards.short_summary: A long-running Northrop concert translating marching-band traditions to an indoor stage.
cards.evidence_claim: Northrop identifies the 2026 program as the 65th annual University of Minnesota Marching Band Indoor Concert.
cards.source_title: 65th Annual Marching Band Indoor Concert at Northrop
cards.access_notes: The official Northrop event page provides date, ticket, and accessibility details for the 2026 concert.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Minnesota-Twin Cities, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-stakes, under-21-friendly first-weekend route through campus landmarks, study spaces, arts, and student resources.

cards.title: Start with the Goldy Gopher Statue
cards.subtitle: Outside Coffman Memorial Union
cards.notes: Meet your new people at the bronze statue, take a quick group photo, then use Coffman as the anchor for the rest of your East Bank walk.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable campus meeting point and photo stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says the six-foot-tall Goldy Gopher statue was unveiled outside Coffman Union in 2013.
cards.source_title: Goldy Gopher | University of Minnesota
cards.access_notes: Outdoor statue outside Coffman Memorial Union.

cards.title: Get Oriented at Coffman Memorial Union
cards.subtitle: 300 Washington Avenue SE
cards.notes: Use the building directory to find the U Card Office, Great Hall, food options, and student resources before splitting off to explore nearby campus.
cards.short_summary: A central union with services, food, and gathering spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Coffman Memorial Union's official directory lists the U Card Office, Great Hall, Goldy's Gameroom, and multiple dining locations.
cards.source_title: Coffman Memorial Union | Student Unions and Activities
cards.access_notes: Check the union's current building-hours page before visiting; U Card access may be required outside public hours.

cards.entity_name: University of Minnesota Bookstores at Coffman Memorial Union
cards.title: Browse the Coffman Bookstore
cards.subtitle: Ground level of Coffman Memorial Union
cards.notes: Take a no-rush lap through the general and academic titles, supplies, and campus merchandise; buy only what you actually need for the term.
cards.short_summary: A campus bookstore inside Coffman with books, supplies, and Gopher items.
cards.evidence_claim: The official bookstore page places the store on Coffman Union's ground level and lists books, course materials, supplies, and University merchandise.
cards.source_title: Coffman Memorial Union | U of M Bookstores
cards.access_notes: Located at 300 Washington Ave SE; confirm current store hours on the official page.

cards.title: Walk Across Northrop Mall
cards.subtitle: East Bank campus green
cards.notes: Walk the mall slowly and point out the buildings you will recognize later; pause on the grass or paths for a simple campus-orientation reset.
cards.short_summary: A signature East Bank green framed by major campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The University's campus-visit page specifically identifies studying in the grass of Northrop Mall as part of the Minneapolis campus experience.
cards.source_title: University of Minnesota Campus Visits
cards.access_notes: Outdoor mall; access and conditions vary with weather and campus operations.

cards.title: Look Inside Northrop
cards.subtitle: Northrop Mall
cards.notes: Check the events calendar for a performance, talk, film, or workshop, and find a study lounge if you want a calm indoor place to regroup.
cards.short_summary: A campus venue for performances, talks, films, and study space.
cards.evidence_claim: Northrop says students gather there for performances, lectures, concerts, film screenings, ceremonies, and other activities; it also has student study lounges.
cards.source_title: U of M Students | Northrop
cards.access_notes: Event entry and prices vary. Consult Northrop's current calendar and event page before attending.

cards.title: Settle into Walter Library
cards.subtitle: East Bank
cards.notes: Find a seat for a brief planning session: compare schedules, make a course-material list, and bookmark library help before your first full week begins.
cards.short_summary: A historic East Bank library and practical first-week study stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Walter Library opened as the University's main library in 1924 and is documented by the University Libraries as a Roman Renaissance-style building.
cards.source_title: Walter Library building history | University of Minnesota Libraries
cards.access_notes: A U Card is required to access campus libraries; consult the Libraries' current hours before going.

cards.title: See the Weisman Art Museum
cards.subtitle: 333 East River Road
cards.notes: Choose one gallery or exhibition to explore at your own pace, then step outside to notice the building and river-facing campus setting.
cards.short_summary: A university art museum with free gallery admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Weisman Art Museum states that admission is always free and that everyone is welcome.
cards.source_title: Weisman Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Verify current gallery hours and any event registration requirements before visiting.

cards.title: Cross the Washington Avenue Bridge
cards.subtitle: Between East Bank and West Bank
cards.notes: Walk across in daylight with your group, pause only where pedestrian traffic stays clear, and use the crossing to get a first look at the river corridor.
cards.short_summary: A pedestrian connection between East Bank and the West Bank arts district.
cards.evidence_claim: The University's campus-visit information describes crossing the Mississippi River to reach West Bank and taking in river and natural-park views from the Washington Avenue Bridge.
cards.source_title: University of Minnesota Campus Visits
cards.access_notes: Use designated pedestrian routes and be mindful of weather, bicycles, and other bridge users.

cards.title: Check Out the Recreation and Wellness Center
cards.subtitle: 123 SE Harvard Street
cards.notes: Stop by to orient yourself to the fitness, climbing, court, and lounge options; save a class or activity idea for a later visit with your U Card.
cards.short_summary: A large East Bank recreation facility with fitness and activity spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: RecWell identifies its East Bank facility at 123 SE Harvard St and lists fitness centers, climbing and bouldering walls, courts, gymnasiums, and an esports lab.
cards.source_title: Hours + Locations | Recreation and Wellness
cards.access_notes: Facility access depends on membership; fee-paying students have automatic membership with a valid U Card.

cards.title: Plan a St. Paul Campus Visit to the Bell Museum
cards.subtitle: 2088 Larpenteur Avenue West, St. Paul
cards.notes: Save this for a daytime outing: explore the natural-history exhibits, planetarium offerings, and outdoor learning landscape, then check transit or shuttle details first.
cards.short_summary: A St. Paul campus natural-history museum and planetarium.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bell Museum describes itself as Minnesota's official natural history museum and planetarium on the University of Minnesota Twin Cities campus in Saint Paul.
cards.source_title: Welcome to the Bell Museum
cards.access_notes: The museum lists Tuesday-Sunday hours; admission prices and planetarium availability should be checked before visiting.
